subject: SLA template: uptime commitment, credit calculation, and pilot credit cap
messages:
From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: alex.jenkins@crescentanalytics.com, procurement@crescentanalytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template: uptime commitment, credit calculation, and pilot credit cap

Hi Alex / Crescent procurement team,

Thanks for the time last week — following up with a focused SLA template for the production rollout. Attached is SLA_Draft_Redwood_v3.pdf (redlines in tracker view). Key points in this draft:

- Standard availability commitment: 99.95% monthly uptime (measured across customer-region endpoints).
- Remedy: monthly service credit calculated as a percentage of that month’s Redwood invoice for the affected services:
  - 99.95%–99.90%: 5% credit of monthly charges
  - 99.89%–99.50%: 15% credit
  - <99.50%: 50% credit, capped at 50% of the monthly invoice
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance (48–72h notice) and emergency maintenance with best-effort notice; both excluded from uptime calc.
- Pilot phase exception: for the first 90 days, we can offer a reduced credit cap of 25% to limit your exposure while we stabilize traffic patterns.

Questions for you: would Crescent accept the 99.95% baseline with the 90-day pilot cap, or do you need a lower baseline (e.g., 99.9%) and a different credit ladder? Also, please indicate the procurement contact for DOCS/PO steps so we can prepare DocuSign.

Attached: SLA_Draft_Redwood_v3.pdf

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

From: alex.jenkins@crescentanalytics.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@crescentanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime commitment, credit calculation, and pilot credit cap

Chloe — thanks for the draft and the clear breakdown. A couple of constraints from our side:

1) Baseline: For our risk model, we typically price around a 99.9% availability baseline for early pilots. Moving to 99.95% materially changes our amortized costs. Is Redwood open to 99.9% for the first 6 months?
2) Credit cap: We appreciate the pilot cap proposal, but procurement prefers a single-digit cap (10% max) for pilot contracts.
3) Batched inference caveat: Our batch workloads will run nightly (00:00–04:00 PT). We need explicit language clarifying that scheduled batch processing windows and any queued processing latencies during that window are not considered service outages unless they exceed agreed SLAs for job start latency.

Attached our procurement questionnaire (Crescent_procurement_questionnaire.pdf) — many of the security/compliance answers are filled. The legal team will review the DocuSign once SLA metrics are finalized.

If it's easier, happy to hop on a 30-min call to get to a final number.

Best,
Alex Jenkins
Director of Platform Engineering
Crescent Analytics
alex.jenkins@crescentanalytics.com | +1 646-555-0128

From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: alex.jenkins@crescentanalytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, procurement@crescentanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime commitment, credit calculation, and pilot credit cap

Alex — really helpful detail, thank you.

On the baseline: we can be pragmatic. Proposal: keep the platform baseline at 99.95% for production customers, but offer Crescent a phased baseline for the pilot: 99.90% for the first 90 days (not six months), then move to 99.95% thereafter assuming normal traffic patterns. That tracks toward your request but shortens exposure for Redwood.

On the credit cap: we can offer a two-tier approach:
- Pilot (first 90 days): credit cap 15% of monthly charges (compromise between our standard cap and your 10% ask).
- Post-pilot: standard cap 50% (as in the SLA draft).

On batched inference: we will add explicit language clarifying scheduled batch windows (00:00–04:00 PT) are excluded from outage calculations provided jobs are accepted and run within agreed job-start SLAs; if job-start latency exceeds the agreed threshold (we propose 30 minutes for batch jobs during the window), it will be treated as an incident. Can you confirm whether 30 minutes is acceptable?

If you confirm the 90-day pilot baseline and the 15% pilot cap, we will:
- Update SLA_Draft_Redwood_v3.pdf with the pilot carveout language and batch-job clause,
- Prepare a DocuSign envelope containing the SLA and SOW addendum for signature (I'll loop Legal if needed),
- Provide a link to the HubSpot deal for procurement to attach your PO (link below).

"On Mon, Jun 25, 2028 at 11:03 AM Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@crescentanalytics.com> wrote:"
> Chloe — thanks for the draft and the clear breakdown. A couple of constraints from our side:
>
> 1) Baseline: For our risk model, we typically price around a 99.9% availability baseline for early pilots. Moving to 99.95% materially changes our amortized costs. Is Redwood open to 99.9% for the first 6 months?
> 2) Credit cap: We appreciate the pilot cap proposal, but procurement prefers a single-digit cap (10% max) for pilot contracts.
> 3) Batched inference caveat: Our batch workloads will run nightly (00:00–04:00 PT). We need explicit language clarifying that scheduled batch processing windows and any queued processing latencies during that window are not considered service outages unless they exceed agreed SLAs for job start latency.

Thanks — want to loop in Marissa (cc) for approval on the pilot cap. If Marissa is ok, I'll get Legal to prepare the DocuSign.

Thanks again,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: alex.jenkins@crescentanalytics.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@crescentanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime commitment, credit calculation, and pilot credit cap

Chloe / Marissa — that compromise looks workable. Two quick confirmations from Crescent:

1) 90-day pilot baseline at 99.90% — agreed.
2) Pilot credit cap 15% — agreed.
3) Batch job acceptance SLA: 30-minute job-start latency during the 00:00–04:00 window is acceptable; any breach escalates as an incident.

Please send the updated SLA (with the pilot carveout and the batch clause) and the DocuSign link. Procurement will route the DocuSign to legal and finance for signature/PO processing. Looking forward to the kick-off next week.

Regards,
Alex Jenkins
Director of Platform Engineering
Crescent Analytics

Attachments referenced: DocuSign envelope pending link; Crescent_procurement_questionnaire.pdf (already attached in earlier mail).
